clue.text: Be prepared for six-footer that is drinking beer in court

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so one piece goes within another
to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: an insect has six legs, and an ant is an insect
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
IPA is India pale ale, a type of beer
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone braces for a giant in a courtroom who is knocking back beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a very tall person, but it counts legs: any insect has six. Two nested containers follow, the beer inside the court and both inside 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to expect it and get ready in advance, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dry run without help – quite the opposite

indicators.note: 'without' can mean outside of, so one piece wraps around another
this phrase flips the instruction just given, so the roles of inner and outer swap

blocks.note: aid is assistance
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A rehearsal held with no assistance, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the run would go outside the help; the tail says do the opposite, so the help goes round the run. 'Dry run' looks like one phrase but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid describes land or climate with almost no rainfall, a direct synonym for parched.

clue.text: Vibration of mobile regularly going off on board plane, say

indicators.note: letters at regular intervals going away leaves every other letter behind
something on board a vessel is inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word
the plane is a kind of tree, so 'say' marks an example

explanation.surface: A phone buzzing in flight mode on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, with 'on board' completing the picture, but it is the plane tree. 'Going off' sounds like the phone ringing; it removes the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremble is a slight shaking movement, so as a noun it matches a vibration.

clue.text: Dairy product the grocer creates with no rights for distribution

indicators.note: having none of something means those letters are taken away
distributing things spreads them about, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right; plural, so every R goes

explanation.surface: A dairy item that a shopkeeper makes but has no licence to sell on.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs leave thirteen letters, exactly the length needed, before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage cheese is a soft, lumpy white curd cheese, an example of something made from milk.

clue.text: Parts of manifesto – 11th idea succeeded!

blocks.note: a plan is an idea or scheme
K is the eleventh letter of the alphabet
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A party's policy document comes together after a last-minute brainwave pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: '11th idea' reads as a numbered proposal; it is the eleventh letter, and that letter follows the idea in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a plank is one policy commitment within a party platform, so several make up parts of a programme.

clue.text: Getting some fruit to friends gathering round

indicators.note: to gather something in is to take it inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: taken as written
mates are friends
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Bringing fruit over to pals who are standing in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering round' looks like friends forming a group, but 'round' is the letter shaped like a circle and 'gathering' puts it inside the friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically tomatoes are fruits, berries of the plant, though usually cooked as vegetables.

clue.text: Old policeman guards shop

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a cop is a police officer
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A retired bobby keeps watch over a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old policeman' reads as one person, but 'Old' is its own abbreviation sitting inside the officer. The Co-op is a British chain of cooperative stores.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-op is a cooperative store, and in Britain the Co-op is a familiar chain of grocery shops.

clue.text: Unfinished fountain pens – a medium for art?

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped
to pen something is to shut it in an enclosure, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a fountain can be a source or origin, as in a fountain of knowledge
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Half-made fountain pens offered as an artist's materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fountain pens' reads as one object; split, the fountain is a source, and 'pens' encloses the next two letters. The question mark flags paper folding as a slightly whimsical art.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes, an example of a decorative art form.

clue.text: Constable maybe making addict finally put down e.g. morphine

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept
making one thing into another means swapping it out for the replacement

blocks.note: John Constable was an English landscape artist
last letter of the word
to put down an animal is to kill it

explanation.surface: A police officer sedating a drug user with an opiate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests a police officer, but it is John Constable, the English painter. The T in that word is replaced by a verb meaning to destroy an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is an opioid used to relieve severe pain, an example of an analgesic drug.

clue.text: Idleness after work – I earn it

indicators.note: once worked over, material has been reshaped, so these letters come out in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone justifies lazing about after the office: they've earned the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' sounds like time off from the job, but it tells you the following letters are worked into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay inactive or unchanging, so it covers sloth or lethargy.

clue.text: With pound on the counter can I drink?

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the word runs the opposite way

blocks.note: to ram is to pound or strike hard
a tin is a can
taken as written

explanation.surface: A customer puts a pound coin on the bar and asks for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money and 'counter' a bar top; the pound is a verb, and the counter sends it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Be fourth when Liberal politician gets luck

indicators.note: being liberal means taking freedoms, so the letters are treated freely and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a Green is a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: An election result: a Lib Dem candidate comes fourth and calls it bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal politician' reads as one person, but 'Liberal' with 'when' is the anagram signal and 'politician' alone is the party member.
explanation.definitionFit: The rub of the green, a phrase from golf, is chance fortune good or bad beyond a player's control.

clue.text: TV show and film you initially ignore

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a film is a thin covering layer, like a blanket of snow
first letter of the word
to blank someone is to ignore them deliberately

explanation.surface: Advice on which television and cinema to skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie but is a covering layer. Blankety Blank is a long-running British TV game show where celebrities fill gaps in phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Blankety Blank is the name of a British television quiz programme, so the answer is an example of a broadcast entertainment.

clue.text: Cook prevailed upon waiter – at last someone who'll get oysters

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged
at last means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word counts

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chef persuades a waiter to fetch the oyster order at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' paints a kitchen scene with the waiter, but it signals rearrangement; the definition stays in the restaurant theme with oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl diver swims down to collect oysters from the sea bed in search of pearls, so it is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Getting no love, reprobate Musk acquires X and I ...

indicators.note: having none of a thing means it is taken out, and acquiring fills the gap
to acquire is to take on something new, which fills the gap left behind

blocks.note: Elon Musk, the tech billionaire
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
Eve was cast out of Eden by God, a reprobate in the biblical sense

explanation.surface: A scoundrel billionaire with no affection buys the platform X, and the speaker too.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the social network Musk bought, which makes it look part of the story; here X and I are Roman numerals. The ellipsis carries the sentence into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals X is ten and I is one, so XI written together stands for the number eleven.

clue.text: ... I leave, displaying obstinacy

blocks.note: one's own self is what 'I' refers to
to will something is to leave it to someone in a testament

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the speaker walks out in a stubborn huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like departing, but it is bequeathing in a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-will is stubborn insistence on getting one's own way, the same quality as pig-headed stubbornness.

clue.text: Weight of drug – speed – unchanged

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
mph, miles per hour, measures speed
as is means left in its present state

explanation.surface: A note on a pure dose of amphetamine, measured by weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' next to 'drug' reads as amphetamine, but it is the unit of velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: To give weight to a point is to stress it, so weight is a synonym for importance or stress.

clue.text: Others in care facility

blocks.note: the rest means the others
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Other people living in a nursing home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a connecting word, but it supplies letters: being in means being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residence where elderly or infirm people are looked after, a type of nursing establishment.

clue.text: In retirement perhaps Diana is eating cold cut

indicators.note: whatever eats takes something inside it, so one piece goes within another
retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Diana Ross, lead singer of the Supremes
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A retired woman called Diana eats a slice of cold meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold cut' looks like sliced meat; 'cold' goes inside, and 'cut' is the definition. Diana is an example of someone surnamed Ross, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor is to snip with shears or blades, so as a verb it means much the same as slice.

clue.text: Cunning plan – gasp!

blocks.note: first meaning: a clever scheme or trick, British informal
second meaning: to breathe with a whistling, laboured sound

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts look like a scheme met with shock; they are separate meanings. In British slang a wheeze is a clever idea or ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is schoolboy slang for a crafty scheme, and the verb describes noisy, laboured breathing.

clue.text: Space on train for bathroom

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
a train or suite is a group of attendants following someone

explanation.surface: A railway passenger looking for room to use the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests a railway, but it is a retinue; in a down clue the space sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a private bathroom attached directly to a bedroom, as in hotel rooms.

clue.text: 007 stated two diamonds must be hidden in potted plant

indicators.note: what is put out of sight is gone from view, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: 007 is James Bond's code number
said means stated
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Bond explained that two gems must be concealed in a flowerpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' looks like jewels for a spy story; it is the card suit, and each of the two words loses one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree grown in a shallow pot, so it is a kind of container plant.

clue.text: Low-footfall food outlets force personnel into difficult situations at the outset

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: to drive is to force or urge
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
tough means difficult
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Quiet fast-food shops drive staff into hard times from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult situations' reads as one phrase, but it splits into an adjective and a single letter. 'Low-footfall' is fair because customers stay in their cars rather than walking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-through serves customers at a window while they sit in their cars, so few people walk through the door.

clue.text: Corporation handling large excess

indicators.note: to handle something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: corporation is old humorous slang for a paunch or belly
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big company dealing with too much stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a company, but it is an old jokey word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, more of something than is needed, so it equals a surplus.

clue.text: Loves person hosting evensong

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the letters are found inside the words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone loves the person who runs the evening church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosting' looks like leading a service, but it signals the letters held within the two preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening prayer service of the Christian church, the same as the Anglican evening service.

clue.text: Extra dish spies used to intercept signal virtually

indicators.note: intercepting cuts into the path of something, so one piece is set within another
virtually means almost entirely, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to spell trouble is to signal or portend it
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Agents eavesdrop on a message about a bonus plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' looks like a radio transmission for spies to tap, but it is a verb meaning to portend, cut short by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A special is a dish offered in addition to the regular menu, such as the chef's daily recommendation.

clue.text: Oddly agree on Republican choice

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Strangely, people concur with a Republican selection.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B places A after B. 'Choice' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning of top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, choice and rare both describe something unusually fine and excellent in quality.

clue.text: Job of librarian – essentially messing around with books

indicators.note: the essence of something is its heart, so the central letter is taken
turned around means moved about, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the middle letter of the nine
taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A librarian's work boils down to fiddling with books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing around' reads as one idiom, but the first word is the material and the second the signal. 'Books' here are biblical, not library stock.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignment is a task allotted to someone, so it is a synonym for a piece of work.
